summary: This entry consolidates the evolution of the USSIF integrity engine, the adoption of RGSD for planning stability, and the transition from brittle snippet-matching to AST-aware patching. It marks the shift toward proactive semantic gating and structural verification, ensuring all self-modifications are validated for soundness while eliminating planning drift and reporting bottlenecks through refined metrics.
key_learnings: Centralizing self-modification logic into an integrity engine with AST-aware patching and post-patch verification prevents silent failures.
Recursive Goal-State Decomposition (RGSD) eliminates logic drift by formalizing sub-goals with feasibility predicates.
System stability is maximized by prioritizing structural readiness over raw throughput and replacing brittle JSON metrics with specific architectural outputs.
Semantic sqlite-vec caching and regex-based pattern matching provide more robust intent-aware state retrieval than hard-coded snippets.
